1) Immediate (30–90 min):
- Token-level request traces for the 08:30-09:15 PT window (request_id, route, latency, status_code). We can export as gzipped NDJSON.
- Per-host runtime metrics (GPU utilization, mem, queue length) aggregated to 1-min buckets and a quick throughput chart (PNG).

2) Next (2–6 hours):
- S3 snapshot of the raw trace bucket + signed SHA256 manifest. We can initiate an S3 object-level snapshot and generate checksums. Expect ~3–4 hours for export and manifest generation depending on object size.
- If customer needs tamper-evidence, we can notarize manifest with our internal signing key and optionally push to a customer-provisioned cloud KMS for verifiable signatures.

3) Constraints and notes:
- Raw request logs contain user identifiers and partial payment tokens — we must coordinate redaction.
- We do retain tracing and runtime metrics for 90 days by default; full raw traces are on S3 for 180 days for this class of account.

Attachments: sre_snapshot_instructions.txt (internal runbook to produce the snapshot and manifest)

Action items for SRE: David / Sean — please start the snapshot job and generate an estimated size. If we need to pull a subset (booking checkout routes only), tell us the expected reduction.

Team,

Legal notes for evidence handling before any external sharing:

1) Put an immediate legal hold on all artifacts in scope (trace buckets, request logs, routing events) — DO NOT DELETE or ROTATE. Document the hold with time, owner and scope.

2) PII / PCI: we must not share raw logs that contain full payment tokens or unredacted customer PII. Recommended path: produce a time-aligned sanitized export (mask PAN fragments, hash user IDs with a salt stored in our HSM) for exec view. For forensic/legal use we can provide hashed/signed raw traces under an NDA amendment; coordinate with their legal team.

3) Tamper-evidence: manifest + SHA256 checksums is fine; for higher assurance we can sign the manifest with our HSM-backed key and provide the public cert chain. Note: notarization with a third-party ledger will take longer.

4) Chain-of-custody: capture who pulled the data, command-line timestamps, and S3 job ids. Attach the signed manifest and include operator usernames.

Please CC me on any outbound that shares artifacts. Marcus — once you have the snapshot ETA, I will draft a short legal-hold notice to attach to the manifest.

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
